intro: The zero conditional (If you heat ice, it melts) describes what always happens when a condition is true: laws of nature, habits, rules and instructions. It uses the present simple in both parts.
objectifs: Build the zero conditional with if / when + present simple, present simple.
Use it for scientific facts, habits, rules and instructions.
Tell it apart from the first conditional (one specific future situation).
Use an imperative or a modal in the result for instructions.

texte: Condition: if (or when, whenever) + present simple. Result: present simple. Both parts are in the present because this is not a single event: it is true every time.
If can almost always be replaced by when or whenever without changing the meaning: “If / When you mix red and blue, you get purple.” This is the easiest test for a zero conditional.

lignes: If I drink coffee after 6 p.m.,

texte: This is the best-known use: laws of nature and facts that are always true. It is very common in science, geography and economics lessons.
The structure is simple; the usual trap is adding will by mistake, or forgetting the -s of the third person.
exemples: If you heat ice, it melts.
Plants die if they don't get enough light.
When demand rises, prices go up.

texte: We also use it for what always happens to us, our habits or reactions: “If I'm stressed, I eat chocolate.” It isn't a universal law, but it's true for me every time.
For a past habit, put both verbs in the past simple: “When I was a child, if it rained, we stayed inside and played cards.”
exemples: If I don't have breakfast, I feel tired all morning.
My grandmother gets angry if we arrive late.
When we lived in Garoua, if it was too hot, we slept on the terrace.
Past habit: past simple in both parts.

sections.titre: Rules and instructions: imperatives and modals
texte: To give a general instruction, the result is often an imperative: “If the alarm rings, leave the building.” You see this on signs, in manuals and in rules.
We can also use a modal (can, must, should): “If you are under 18, you can't vote.” / “If you feel dizzy, you should sit down.”

lignes: If there is a fire, don't use the lift.
If the light turns red, press the reset button.
If you lose your card, you must pay a fee.
If you have a fever, drink plenty of water.

texte: Zero: true every time, in general (present + present). First: one specific situation in the future (present + will).
“If you press this button, the machine stops” (that's how it always works). “If you press this button now, the machine will stop” (now, this one time).
A useful signal: if you can say “whenever” or “every time”, it's a zero conditional. With tomorrow, tonight or next week, it's a first conditional.
exemples: If you mix oil and water, they don't combine.
If you mix these colours, your painting will look dark.
This time, a predicted result: first.

formule: If / When + present simple, present simple (If you heat ice, it melts.)
prononciation: The third-person -s is necessary and must be heard: melts /melts/, boils /bɔɪlz/, rises /ˈraɪzɪz/. Three sounds: /s/, /z/, /ɪz/.
when /wen/ and if /ɪf/ are often weak at the start; the stress falls on the important verbs and nouns: “If you HEAT ICE, it MELTS.”
Intonation: rising at the end of the condition, falling at the end of the result.
whenever /wenˈevə/: stress on the second syllable.
erreurs: If you heat the ice, it melts.
If you heat ice, it melts.
General truth: no article before an uncountable noun used in a general sense.
If water freeze, it become ice.
If water freezes, it becomes ice.
When I will be tired, I go to bed.
When I'm tired, I go to bed.
If you will press the button, the door opens.
If you press the button, the door opens.
If it rains, people are taking umbrellas.
If it rains, people take umbrellas.
A general habit: present simple, not present continuous.
If there will be a fire, use the stairs.
If there is a fire, use the stairs.

dialogue.contexte: A science class in a secondary school in Liège. Ms Dubois explains an experiment to her students, Théo and Aïcha.
lignes: What happens if you put salt on ice?
A question about a general truth.
Exactly. That's why the city puts salt on the roads when it snows.
And if the temperature is very low, does salt still work?
Good question. If it's colder than about minus ten, salt doesn't work very well.
In Cameroon, my cousins never see snow. If it rains a lot, the roads just get muddy.
Get muddy = become covered in mud.
That's right. Now, safety first: if you spill anything, tell me immediately.
And if we finish early, can we try with sugar?

exercices.consigne: Match the beginnings and endings: a) it turns into steam. b) I get a headache. c) you get green. d) leave the building.
items: If you mix blue and yellow, …
c) you get green.
If water boils, …
a) it turns into steam.
If I don't drink enough water, …
b) I get a headache.
If the fire alarm rings, …
d) leave the building.

exercices.titre: 2. Put the verbs in the right form
exercices.consigne: Put the verbs in the present simple (zero conditional).
items: If you ___ (drop) a glass, it ___ (break).
drop … breaks
When my phone battery ___ (be) low, the screen ___ (get) darker.
is … gets
If people ___ (not / sleep) enough, they ___ (feel) irritable.
don't sleep … feel
My dog ___ (bark) if someone ___ (ring) the bell.
barks … rings
If you ___ (not / pay) the bill, they ___ (cut) the electricity.
don't pay … cut
If you heat metal, it (expands / will expand). (always)
expands
If you call me tonight, I (tell / will tell) you everything.
will tell
When I'm nervous, I (talk / will talk) too much.
talk
If it rains tomorrow, the match (is / will be) cancelled.
will be

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: If you press this button, the machine stop.
If you press this button, the machine stops.
When the sun will set, it gets cold in the desert.
When the sun sets, it gets cold in the desert.
If there will be an emergency, call 112.
If there is an emergency, call 112.
If my brother is hungry, he is getting angry.
If my brother is hungry, he gets angry.

exercices.consigne: Write a zero conditional sentence from the prompts.
items: heat ice / melt
If you heat ice, it melts.
when / I / drink coffee in the evening / not sleep
When I drink coffee in the evening, I don't sleep. / I can't sleep.
lose your ticket / must / pay a fine
If you lose your ticket, you must pay a fine.
have a fever / drink a lot of water (imperative)
If you have a fever, drink a lot of water.

exercices.consigne: Write 4 zero conditional sentences: a scientific fact, one of your habits, a rule at your school or workplace, and a safety instruction (imperative).
items: Example answer

If you freeze water, it turns into ice. If I go to bed late, I feel tired the next day. At my company, if you work on Saturday, you get a day off. If you smell gas, open the windows and leave the house.

a_retenir: If / When + present simple, present simple: what always happens.
Uses: laws of nature, habits, rules, instructions.
If can be replaced by when / whenever without changing the meaning.
Use an imperative or a modal in the result for instructions.
One specific future situation → first conditional (will).
